title: Model registry: persist tiered batching defaults (by model family, optional GPU SKU) with versioning + rollout gates
author: Ethan Park
description: Summary: This adds first-class storage for tiered batching defaults in the model registry so we can ship workload-aware batching tiers (fast/standard/cost_efficient) with auditability, versioning, and safe rollout toggles. Defaults are keyed by model_family, with an optional gpu_sku scope when we need different knobs for memory/throughput differences. Motivation: The runtime is gaining tier-based mapping logic (ENG-18421) and config surfaces (PRs in redwood). We need a single source of truth for tier defaults that (a) can be updated independently of runtime deploys, (b) supports canary/percent rollouts by model+region, (c) is auditable for enterprise change management, and (d) allows SKU-specific overrides without forking full model configs. What’s in this PR: 1) New registry object: batching_tier_defaults. Each entry stores parameters per tier, with optional overrides by gpu_sku. 2) Versioning: entries are immutable once published; updates create a new version (semver-like string + incrementing integer). Includes created_by, created_at, change_summary, and optional links to benchmark artifacts. 3) Rollout gates: per version, we can set rollout policy fields used by the control plane/routing layer: enabled (bool), enabled_percent (0-100), and allowlist/denylist filters (regions, customer_tiers) serialized as strings; these are intentionally conservative for beta. 4) Read APIs: GET /v1/model-families/{family}/batching-tier-defaults returns the latest effective version plus the computed effective config for an optional gpu_sku. Also added a lightweight “explain” shape to support Console’s effective-config view (ties into redwood PR 18470). 5) Validation + migration: registry validation ensures max_queue_delay_ms bounds and tier presence; includes a one-time backfill script for initial model families (llama3*, mistral*, qwen2*) with placeholder values aligned to current benchmark sweeps. Notes/constraints: - Precedence is unchanged: explicit customer config still wins; tier defaults only apply when batching_tier is set and the user hasn’t overridden the specific knob. - SKU override is only used when present; otherwise we fall back to model_family defaults. - Rollout gates are registry-level primitives; the actual percent-based enablement enforcement remains in the runtime/control-plane flag system. This PR just persists the desired policy so it can be audited and reasoned about. Testing: unit tests for schema validation + version immutability, integration tests for GET endpoints (latest + by version), and a “resolve effective defaults” test matrix across tiers and gpu_sku overrides. Ops: emits audit log events for publish/update actions (who/what/when) and exports registry metrics: model_registry_tier_defaults_resolve_errors_total and model_registry_tier_defaults_version_published_total. Example entry (illustrative): model_family=llama3.1-70b, version=1.0.1, gpu_sku overrides for A10G vs H100 to adjust kv_cache_pressure_limit and max_batch_size on cost_efficient tier.
commits: registry/storage: add versioned persistence layer + immutability guard
api: GET endpoints for tier defaults + effective resolution
rollout: persist rollout gate fields + audit log events
scripts: backfill initial model families with v1 entries
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can we tighten validation on max_queue_delay_ms for fast tier? I’d like an upper bound so we don’t accidentally ship 50ms in fast and break token cadence. Also, can resolveEffectiveTierDefaults expose whether a value came from sku override vs family default (for debugging)?

Ethan Park (author): Added bounds in validator: fast.max_queue_delay_ms <= 8ms, standard <= 20ms, cost_efficient <= 60ms (still configurable per family). Also updated resolver to return a debug string field (source_map) that annotates each knob with family|sku and version. Kept it behind a query param include_debug=true to avoid bloating default responses.

Benji Okafor (review): Rollout gates: please clarify semantics of enabled vs enabled_percent. If enabled=false, do we ignore enabled_percent? Also need to ensure defaults are safe if gates are missing (treat as disabled).

Ethan Park (author): Updated docs + handler: if gates missing => disabled. If enabled=false => always disabled regardless of percent. If enabled=true and enabled_percent unset => 100%. Added test coverage for each combination.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics naming: resolve_errors_total is good, but please add a label for model_family and endpoint, and ensure cardinality is bounded (family is bounded but confirm). Also can we emit a counter when we fall back from sku override to family default (helps identify missing SKU coverage)?

Ethan Park (author): Added labels: model_family, endpoint. Also added counter model_registry_tier_defaults_sku_fallback_total{model_family,gpu_sku}. gpu_sku label is bounded by our known SKUs (A10G/L4/A100/H100) and validated against an allowlist in the request handler.
Jonas Weber (review): Please include an optional field for linking benchmark artifacts (drive doc or benchmark-lab run id). We’ll want to enforce that in process later even if not required now.

Ethan Park (author): Added optional benchmark_ref string and benchmark_ref_type enum-ish string ("benchmark-lab-run" | "drive-doc" | "other"). Not required by schema; included in API response + audit payload.
Lena Fischer (review): Minor: can we standardize tier naming to cost_efficient (underscore) across schema + API? I saw ‘cost-efficient’ in docs section.

Ethan Park (author): Normalized to cost_efficient everywhere in schema and code; updated docs and added a backwards-compat alias in request parsing for cost-efficient just in case (returns warning header).
Sofia Ivanova (review): Looks good after changes. Approving.
Benji Okafor (review): Approving once CI is green on rerun (saw transient integration failure).
Ethan Park (author): Reran integration-tests; was a flaky port bind. Green now.
release_notes: Internal: model registry now supports versioned tier-default storage (fast/standard/cost_efficient) scoped by model family with optional GPU SKU overrides; includes rollout gate fields and audit logging for publish/update actions.
